strategy.observation: Plausible sells a privacy-focused, open-source analytics product and also offers white-label and self-hosted options for teams that need analytics built into their own products.
strategy.offer_link: Paid search campaigns could help Plausible capture high-intent queries from SaaS platforms, website builders, and privacy-conscious buyers looking for analytics alternatives, white-label analytics, or self-hosted analytics.
hypotheses: You may be looking to grow qualified inbound demand from buyers already searching for privacy-safe analytics.
Search could be a meaningful channel because your white-label and self-hosted offers likely map to specific commercial keywords.
A paid search program might be used to support partner-style or platform-level sales motions, not just direct-to-self-serve signups.
strategy.angle: Plausible already sells privacy-first analytics plus white-label and self-hosted options, so search could be a way to capture buyers actively looking for those exact terms.
strategy.fit_reason: The offer matches Plausible’s category closely: it is a privacy-focused software product, and its white-label/self-hosted positioning creates clear search-intent keywords that paid search can target.

draft.subject: Search for analytics demand
draft.body:
Plausible already sells privacy-focused, open source analytics, and it also has white-label and self-hosted options. That should map to search terms like privacy-friendly analytics, white-label analytics, and self-hosted analytics.

I run paid search campaigns for privacy-focused software products. Would it make sense to test a small search program around those terms and see if it brings qualified demand from SaaS platforms and website builders?
